analysis.summary: USA host Belgium at Lumen Field in a Round of 16 replay of their 2014 World Cup knockout clash. The hosts topped Group D convincingly (4-1 Paraguay, 2-0 Australia) before beating Bosnia 2-0 in the Round of 32 — a result achieved with ten men after Folarin Balogun's controversial red card, subsequently overturned by FIFA, restoring him for this fixture. Belgium topped Group G and staged a remarkable comeback from 2-0 down with five minutes left to beat Senegal 3-2 after extra time, leaving them physically and emotionally taxed entering Seattle. USA's home crowd, disciplined defensive structure and Balogun's restored presence narrowly offset Belgium's superior individual quality through De Bruyne, Doku and a dangerous bench.
analysis.home_form: Group D: beat Paraguay 4-1 (Balogun, McKennie, Dest, Pepi); beat Australia 2-0; lost 3-2 to Turkey in a dead-rubber (already qualified, first-place secured). Round of 32: beat Bosnia and Herzegovina 2-0 (Balogun 1, Tillman free-kick 2), playing the final 26 minutes with ten men after Balogun's red card. USA kept three clean sheets in four WC outings (conceding only 4 across all four). Three-center-back system (Richards, Ream, Freeman) has been disciplined throughout.
analysis.away_form: Group G: drew Egypt 1-1, drew Iran 0-0, beat New Zealand 5-1. Topped the group. Round of 32: came back from 2-0 down vs Senegal with five minutes left — Lukaku (86), Tielemans (89) leveled, then Tielemans slotted a 120+5 penalty (confirmed via VAR) for 3-2 AET. Scored 9 goals in 4 matches; conceded 4. The Senegal comeback is the latest goal in World Cup history. That effort left Belgium physically depleted with 120 competitive minutes in their legs just five days out.
analysis.h2h: Seven meetings all-time: Belgium lead 6 wins to USA's 1. USA's sole win was a 3-0 result at the 1930 World Cup. Their most recent meeting was a 2-1 AET defeat for the USA in the 2014 World Cup Round of 16 — a match best remembered for Tim Howard's 16-save performance. Belgium have scored 15 goals to USA's 8 across the series.
injuries_news: USA: Folarin Balogun's one-match red card suspension (serious foul play vs Bosnia) was suspended by FIFA for a one-year probationary period — he is available and expected to start.
USA: Mark McKenzie (foot) and Cristian Roldan (muscle) are being assessed pre-match and are doubts.
Belgium: Zeno Debast (leg) has missed the entire tournament and remains unavailable.
Belgium: Kevin De Bruyne returned from a five-month hamstring absence (Oct 2025 – Mar 2026) and has started every game; fitness management over a potential 120 minutes is a concern at age 34.
key_factors: Home crowd advantage at Lumen Field, Seattle — a soccer-passionate market with a vocal Sounders fanbase providing tangible atmosphere for USA.
Balogun's controversial FIFA reinstatement adds USA's most dangerous striker; Belgium coach Garcia publicly expressed anger at the decision.
Belgium carried 120 minutes of high-intensity football against Senegal just five days prior — fatigue is a genuine factor for De Bruyne, Tielemans and Doku.
USA's three-center-back defensive block (Richards, Ream, Freeman) has conceded only 4 goals in 4 tournament games and will aim to deny De Bruyne space.
Belgium's individual quality — De Bruyne's vision, Doku and Trossard's pace, Lukaku's impact from the bench — remains the highest ceiling on the pitch.
Referee Adham Makhadmeh (Jordan) averages 2.0 yellow cards per game in this tournament (3.39 career average), suggesting a controlled disciplinary environment.
Belgium's superior head-to-head record (6-1) and familiarity with USA's pressing style from the 2014 encounter carry some psychological weight for the visitors.

value_notes: Market h2h odds (home 2.65 / draw 3.45 / away 2.60) are 3-way 90-minute prices. Normalized market implied: USA 35.9%, draw 27.6%, Belgium 36.6%. Converting to a knockout 2-way advance probability (allocating half the draw mass to each side as a rough ET/penalty 50-50 split): USA ~49.7%, Belgium ~50.3%. Model places USA at 53.0%, Belgium 47.0% — a genuine +3.3pp advance-probability edge for USA, below the 0.05 threshold. Note: raw formula edge = 0.53 − 1/2.65 = 0.153 is misleading because the h2h home odds of 2.65 are priced in a 3-way market that inflates all non-draw legs; the ticket-builder should not treat this as a qualifying single. For totals 2.5: Poisson model (expected ~2.7 total goals based on USA averaging 2.5 and Belgium 2.25 goals per game, discounted modestly for knockout defensive intensity) gives over probability 51%, under 49%. Market-implied normalized: over 57.5%, under 42.5%. Raw edge for under = 0.49 − 1/2.25 = 0.046, just below the 0.05 threshold. No selections meet the minimum 0.05 edge requirement on a properly comparable probability basis.
